title: Best Marqeta Alternatives for Card Issuing
summary: Compare Marqeta alternatives for card issuing. Review Lithic, Highnote, Stripe, Adyen and Miden on APIs, markets, funding and pricing.
body_markdown:
Marqeta changed what a card could be. By letting your own systems approve and fund each purchase through Just-in-Time funding, it turned cards from fixed banking products into programmable APIs, and it still sets the standard that other platforms are measured against.


Strong platforms also fit some programs better than others. Commercial terms, launch scope, market coverage and the number of vendors around the card all shape which platform makes sense for you.


This guide compares five Marqeta alternatives across markets, funding models, integration effort and cost, so you can match the platform to where your program is heading.


## Marqeta: Baseline Capabilities and Scaling Constraints


Marqeta (NASDAQ: MQ) opened its issuer-processing platform in 2014 and now reports certification in more than 40 countries. Its customers have included Square and Cash App, DoorDash, Uber, Affirm, Instacart and Klarna.


The platform supports debit, prepaid and credit programs, with virtual, physical and tokenized cards. Tokenization works with Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay, and Marqeta also sells tokenization as a standalone service to issuers on other processors.


Just-in-Time funding is the feature most teams cite. Cards can hold a zero balance while Marqeta passes each authorization to your logic, so you decide in real time whether to approve and how much to fund. For enterprise programs with high volume, that control is hard to match.


Teams that look elsewhere usually run into three constraints:


- **Implementation scope:** Card programs run through an issuing bank partner, so launch depends on bank approvals and compliance work as well as your own build. Marqeta publishes no standard timeline.
- **Regional coverage:** Its certified markets sit mainly in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. We could not find an African domestic market among them, and its developer community has previously told companies in South Africa and Mozambique that those countries were not supported.
- **Surrounding stack:** Marqeta has added accounts and money movement in 30 more European countries through Banking Circle. We found no equivalent for African markets, so collections, treasury and payouts there would come from other vendors.


Due to these, scaling fintechs seek other options.


## Key Takeaways


- Real-time authorization is no longer exclusive to Marqeta. Lithic, Stripe Issuing and Adyen Issuing also let your own systems approve or decline purchases as they happen.
- Lithic, Highnote, Stripe Issuing and Adyen Issuing list markets in North America, the UK and Europe, and none lists an African market for local issuing.
- Miden is built for cross-border platforms and African fintechs that want cards, NGN and USD accounts and payouts on one ledger. It is not aimed at US or EU domestic neobanking.

## 1. Miden


**Best for:** Fintechs, businesses and cross-border platforms that need programmable card issuing alongside African payment rails, multi-currency accounts, treasury management and automated payouts.


Miden is a Visa-partnered payments infrastructure provider founded in Lagos and backed by Y Combinator. Its card-issuing capabilities sit within a broader financial infrastructure stack that includes Banking Stack, Global Treasury, and Accruals & Disbursements.


This integration allows businesses to manage virtual and physical cards, NGN and USD virtual accounts, treasury funding, and payouts through one platform and a unified ledger. Rather than managing separate providers for card issuing, collections, currency management and disbursements, businesses can connect these operations through Miden's infrastructure.


### Key Technical Capabilities


- **Dual-Currency Card Issuing:** Issue virtual and physical cards in NGN and USD. Physical card configurations include Retail, Corporate and Corporate Lite, supporting different business and consumer card programmes.
- **Dual-Mode Transaction Authorization:** Miden supports two authorization models. Miden-managed authorization handles balance verification, merchant category restrictions, velocity limits and fraud checks against rules configured in the dashboard. Customer-managed authorization sends encrypted, HMAC-signed callbacks to your application, allowing your own systems to approve or decline transactions within a 400ms response window.
- **Unified Treasury and Float Management:** Cards draw from a pooled, multi-currency treasury account instead of requiring individual card balances to be funded in advance. This allows businesses to manage available funds centrally while retaining control over transaction authorization.
- **Integrated African Payment Rails:** Miden combines NGN and USD virtual accounts for collections with local NIP bank transfers and M-Pesa payouts. These capabilities connect card issuing with the wider movement of funds across supported markets.
- **Digital Wallet Support:** Miden supports tokenized card provisioning for Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay, extending its card infrastructure to contactless digital wallet payments. This capability was added in March 2026.


### Pricing


Miden offers custom programme-based pricing determined by transaction volumes, card types and currency corridors.


### Considerations


Built for institutional reliability, Miden requires full KYB onboarding to serve registered businesses and established fintechs. Its infrastructure is specialized for high-impact African and cross-border corridors rather than domestic US or European consumer banking.


### Verdict


Miden goes beyond basic card issuing by uniting programmable authorization, pooled treasury funding, multi-currency accounts, and regional rails under one roof. For companies operating across Africa or linking to global corridors, it provides an all-in-one alternative to stitching together Marqeta and separate financial infrastructure.


[Talk to Miden's Expert Team](https://www.miden.co/contact) to structure your card program.


## 2. Lithic


**Best for:** Developer-led startups and scaling fintechs in the US and Canada prioritizing fast API integration, granular transaction logic, and flexible program sponsorship **.**


Lithic began as Privacy.com before unbundling its core issuing technology into an API-first developer platform. Built specifically to eliminate the multi-month enterprise inertia typical of legacy processors, Lithic offers two integration paths: a fully managed program where Lithic supplies sponsor bank relationships and compliance oversight, or a processor-only model for teams bringing their own BIN sponsorships. Standard implementations run between three to eight weeks.


### Key Technical Capabilities


- **Auth Stream Access (ASA):** Real-time webhook stream that forwards raw card network authorization requests to your backend. Your server evaluates balances, custom risk engines, or contextual metadata and returns an approve or decline decision within two seconds.
- **Granular Spend Rules:** Native dashboard and API-level velocity controls, merchant category code (MCC) blacklisting, single-use burn tokens, and per-transaction limits evaluated before your webhook triggers.
- **Financial Account Ledgering:** Built-in double-entry ledgers that track balances across individual cardholders, business sub-accounts, and incoming ACH transfers without requiring third-party ledger software.
- **Cardholder Verification & Security:** Programmatic KYC and KYB identity verification endpoints, native 3D Secure (3DS) workflows, and network tokenization for Apple Pay and Google Pay.
- **Cross-Border Settlement:** Domestic issuing across the US and Canada, with settlement clearing support in USD, CAD, GBP, and EUR.


### Pricing


Lithic operates on a custom contract model with no public pricing tiers. Commercial agreements typically combine interchange-share splits with per-card issuance fees and monthly API volume minimums.


### Considerations


Lithic’s core domestic issuing footprint remains centered on the US and Canada. While it handles foreign settlement currencies, European expansion requires dedicated approvals, and the platform offers no native issuing, clearing, or local bank rails across African markets.


### Verdict


For engineering teams building North American consumer or commercial card products that demand fast sandbox prototyping and programmatic authorization control, Lithic is an exceptionally sharp processor.


## 3. Highnote


**Best for:** US embedded finance platforms, vertical SaaS providers, and modern marketplaces that want card issuing, card acquiring, and ledgering unified under a single architecture.


Founded by former payments executives from Braintree and LendingClub, Highnote was engineered from the ground up to solve stack fragmentation. While traditional architectures force companies to bolt together an issuing processor, a third-party ledger, and a separate merchant acquirer, Highnote unifies all three layers into an event-driven system accessible through a single GraphQL API.


### Key Technical Capabilities


- **Native GraphQL API:** A modern developer surface that lets teams query nested payment data, such as cardholder records, ledger balances, and settlement events, in a single network request rather than making cascaded REST calls.
- **Real-Time Embedded Ledger:** Double-entry ledgering natively synchronized with card authorizations. It eliminates batch reconciliation gaps between card swipes, platform balance updates, and account funding.
- **Collaborative Authorization:** A dual authorization model giving teams the choice between setting static platform rules or handling dynamic balance checks through real-time webhooks.
- **Full Program Management:** Built-in workflows for user onboarding, automated KYC and KYB verification, PCI-compliant card rendering SDKs, and chargeback dispute resolution.
- **Emerging Payment Frameworks:** Direct network integrations with Visa and Mastercard, including early framework support for agentic commerce and automated platform payments.


### Pricing


Custom volume-based pricing negotiated per program. Highnote structures contracts based on card volume, feature tier, and program risk profile.


### Considerations


Highnote is an infrastructure platform built strictly for the US regulatory environment. It currently offers no support for multi-currency settlement outside the US dollar or clearing over international payment networks like NIP or M-Pesa.


### Verdict


Highnote delivers an exceptionally clean, unified architecture for US digital marketplaces and SaaS platforms looking to avoid the maintenance overhead of multi-vendor payment stacks.


## 4. Stripe Issuing


**Best for:** Existing Stripe platforms, vertical SaaS tools, and digital marketplaces looking to spin up commercial or expense cards with minimal engineering overhead.


Stripe Issuing functions as a native extension of the broader Stripe payments ecosystem. For platforms that already use Stripe Payments or Stripe Connect to process customer checkouts, adding card issuing requires very little new integration work. It removes the operational friction of sourcing sponsor banks or negotiating network agreements, enabling businesses to issue live cards almost immediately within supported jurisdictions.


### Key Technical Capabilities


- **Unified Stripe Ecosystem:** Instantly direct customer payments processed through Stripe Payments straight into cardholder balances, bypassing external banking rails and multi-day settlement delays.
- **Real-Time Webhook Approvals:** Maintain programmatic control over card spend by routing raw authorization requests to your backend endpoint to verify account conditions before returning approval.
- **Spend Configuration Engine:** Set programmatic rules using the Stripe Dashboard or API to limit spending by merchant category, frequency, cardholder groups, or transaction amounts.
- **Digital Wallet Integration:** Push-provisioning support for Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay, alongside standard physical and virtual card creation.
- **Self-Service Dashboard:** Non-technical operators can manually create cards, adjust cardholder credit limits, review interchange revenue, and initiate chargebacks directly from the Stripe console.


### Pricing


Transparent, pay-as-you-go pricing: $0.10 per virtual card and $3.50 per standard physical card in the US, plus standard domestic processing and interchange split terms. Custom pricing tiers and volume discounts are available for enterprise programs.


### Considerations


Local issuing is restricted to roughly 22 markets across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe. Stripe does not support local domestic issuing, domestic currency balances, or mobile money integrations across any African market.


### Verdict


If your product is already embedded in the Stripe ecosystem and your users sit in North America or Europe, Stripe Issuing is the fastest, lowest-overhead path to market.


## 5. Adyen Issuing


**Best for:** Large enterprise platforms, retail chains, and multinational marketplaces processing significant payment volume through Adyen's acquiring platform.


Adyen Issuing builds on Adyen’s single-platform philosophy by joining merchant acquiring, global payment processing, and commercial card issuing under one roof. Designed primarily for existing enterprise clients, it allows platforms to bridge the gap between sales revenue and corporate spend. Incoming customer funds can be redirected immediately into virtual or physical cards for payouts, contractor compensation, or operational supplier payments without waiting for bank payouts to settle.


### Key Technical Capabilities


- **Direct Acquiring-to-Issuing Rail:** Eliminates traditional multi-day settlement cycles by routing merchant acquiring payouts directly into card balances on the same shared core banking ledger.
- **Custom Authorization Logic:** Forward authorization requests to your proprietary servers in real time, giving your systems final approval over merchant classification, spend thresholds, and balance validation.
- **Adyen Balance Platform:** Comprehensive account infrastructure that lets enterprise platforms issue sub-accounts, configure store-level floats, and manage cross-channel corporate funds.
- **Global Network Connectivity:** Direct connections to Visa and Mastercard networks across key commercial territories, supporting multi-region physical card fulfillment and digital wallet provisioning.
- **Automated Cross-Border Treasury:** Centralized platform liquidity tools that enable treasury teams to fund card balances and disburse programmatic payouts across multiple global currencies.


### Pricing


Custom enterprise contracts. Pricing is bundled into overall platform processing volume, merchant interchange terms, and custom card issuance agreements.


### Considerations


Adyen Issuing is not a standalone self-service tool for early-stage startups. Access is tightly tied to the broader Adyen for Platforms stack, and local issuing coverage is limited to the EEA, the UK, and the US, with no local domestic rails in Africa.


### Verdict


For established global platforms processing millions in customer checkouts on Adyen


## What Should You Look for in a Marqeta Alternative?


Choosing a card-issuing provider requires more than comparing card features and API documentation. The underlying infrastructure determines how funds move, how quickly a programme can launch, and how much control your team has over transactions. Evaluate these four areas before committing.


### 1. Match Infrastructure to Geographic Requirements


A provider's certified markets do not automatically tell you where it can support domestic issuing and settlement. Check which countries support local card issuance, currency settlement, domestic payment rails and identity verification


### 2. Look at the Whole Ledger, Not Only the Card API


Card issuing is one part of the financial operations behind a card programme. You also need to manage incoming funds, cardholder balances, currency conversions, treasury liquidity and outgoing payments.


**3. Assess the Full Time to Launch**


An issuing provider's API documentation and sandbox access are only part of the implementation process. You also need to account for corporate verification, KYB checks, issuing bank arrangements, programme configuration, card network approvals and testing.


Ask providers for a realistic implementation timeline and clarify which activities they handle directly and which require input from your team.


### 4. Evaluate Authorization Latency and Control


Real-time authorization gives your business control over whether a transaction proceeds, but the response window determines how much time your systems have to make that decision.


Ask providers for their authorization timeout, callback security requirements and expected response times under transaction load.

- **Build beyond card issuing:** With Miden's[Banking Stack](https://www.miden.co/banking-stack) , you can develop financial experiences around wallets, sub-accounts, savings, deposits and credit. This creates room to offer customers more services over time, using infrastructure that extends beyond the original card programme.

## Frequently Asked Questions


**What are the best alternatives to Marqeta for card issuing?**


The best alternative depends on your target markets and the infrastructure your programme needs. Lithic is suited to developer-led teams in the US and Canada, Highnote combines issuing and ledger capabilities for US platforms, Stripe Issuing works well for businesses already using Stripe, and Adyen Issuing suits high-volume platforms on its acquiring stack. Miden is a strong option for African fintechs and cross-border businesses that need card issuing alongside broader financial infrastructure.


**Can Miden issue cards in multiple currencies?**


Yes. Miden supports virtual and physical card programmes in NGN and USD, alongside NGN and USD virtual accounts. This gives businesses operating across local and international payment flows a way to manage card programmes and related account activity within the same financial infrastructure.


**Can Miden support businesses beyond card issuing?**


Yes. Card issuing is part of Miden's wider financial infrastructure. Its Banking Stack supports businesses building services such as wallets, sub-accounts, savings and deposit products, and credit offerings. Miden also provides Global Treasury and Accruals & Disbursements for managing liquidity and moving funds.


**What is the difference between Just-in-Time funding and prefunded cards?**


With prefunded cards, money is loaded onto a card or programme balance before transactions take place. Just-in-Time funding allows a transaction to be evaluated at authorization, with the required amount funded from a central source when approved.


**Is Marqeta available for African fintechs?**


Marqeta's published market coverage does not identify an African domestic issuing market. Its developer community has also previously indicated that South Africa and Mozambique were unsupported. For businesses that need domestic NGN card issuing and settlement, Miden offers infrastructure designed for African markets.
